title: Sales/CS Request Normalizer and Stage-Gate for Account Bundles
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Problem: Sales and Customer Success regularly submit multi-item feature asks for enterprise accounts. These arrive as overlapping requests across stakeholders, inconsistent descriptions, and variable technical detail. That causes duplicated scoping work, slow first responses, and mismatched expectations between Product, Eng, and the customer.

Goal: Design and pilot a lightweight normalization + stage-gate pipeline that: 1) consolidates related asks per account into a single ‘bundle’ record, 2) performs a timeboxed first-pass scoping (value, compliance, rough effort), and 3) outputs a clear next-step (Quick-win, Scalable project, or Requires R&D). Deliver a repeatable template, scoring rubric, and a short-run pilot with 3–5 accounts.

Why this matters: Reduces duplicate discovery work for PM/Eng; improves SLA to Sales/CS; surfaces high-impact opportunities faster; and creates structured inputs for roadmap decisions and Dedicated/Private deal sizing.
acceptance_criteria: A canonical intake template (Google Doc) linked from the Sales/CS playbook and used in >=80% of pilot cases
A normalization heuristic that groups related asks into an account bundle with <=3 manual adjustments during pilot
A scoring rubric for business value, technical feasibility, and compliance that yields a clear recommendation in >=90% of pilot bundles
Pilot with 3–5 accounts completed, with documented time-to-first-scoping <=5 business days
Artifacts (bundle matrix, decision log, follow-up tickets) stored in Drive and referenced from each Linear ticket
proposed_workflow: Step 0: Triage - Sales/CS submits item via standardized intake form (link) and tags account + urgency
Step 1: Normalization - Automated pass groups similar items by account and feature theme (NLP-assisted), PM reviews and confirms within 48h
Step 2: First-pass scoping (timeboxed to 3 business days) - PM fills template: customer impact, usage estimate, compliance flags, simple effort band (S/M/L)
Step 3: Scoring - Apply rubric to recommend: Quick-win (<=2 sprints), Roadmap candidate, Requires deep R&D, or Not prioritised
Step 4: Output - Create follow-up artifacts: a short summary to Sales/CS, an Eng intake ticket for accepted items, and a decision log entry
Step 5: Review cadence - Weekly 30-minute intake sync with Sales/CS for edge cases and prioritization escalations
scoring_rubric: Business value: Revenue uplift / retention impact (0-5)
Implementation effort: effort bands mapped to story points (0-5, lower better)
Technical risk: compatibility with serving runtime / data constraints (0-5, lower better)
Compliance/Privacy: flags that require Private/VPC or KMS (0-5)
Overall recommendation: score threshold map to Quick-win / Roadmap / R&D / Reject
